The Power Reckoning

Between August and October 2026 the scarce input for AI data centers stopped being megawatts alone and became permission: permission to connect, to co-locate and to build. Buyers reached for existing nuclear plants, while FERC, PJM and state officials in Texas, North Carolina and Virginia began rewriting who pays and who waits.

By Gilbert (empirical byline, Brand Bible §06) · Evidence window Aug 13, 2026 to Oct 12, 2026 · Status: draft (not signed off)

The argument

Permission has joined power as the constraint

The record in this Briefing is thirty-seven sourced items, Faraday Signals and crawled articles, dated between 13 August and 12 October 2026. Read together, they show two movements happening at once.

The first is a rush to existing nuclear capacity. Google signed a 20-year agreement with Constellation for 890 MW from upgrades at 11 existing units in Illinois, Pennsylvania and New Jersey 1, with Constellation investing over $4.3 billion 2. Amazon signed a 20-year agreement around Calvert Cliffs in Maryland 5. Meta secured up to 6.6 GW from TerraPower, Oklo and Vistra 7. The Department of Energy is lending into the same plants: a conditional $4.2 billion package for Vistra uprates adding 433 MW 6 and a closed $1.9 billion loan to restart Duane Arnold in Iowa 9.

The second is a tightening of the rules for connecting large loads. FERC issued show-cause orders in June 2026 to six grid operators over interconnection rules for loads above 50 MW 18. PJM filed a mechanism that would require new large data center loads to bring qualifying capacity or face backstop procurement 19. Texas paused new data center permits pending an ERCOT audit 28,29. North Carolina regulators refused a Duke Energy gas turbine request on cost and uncertain need 30.

Where those two movements meet, projects slip. Oracle invoked force majeure with STACK Infrastructure over delays at Project Jupiter, citing power supply, air permits and land access 13, and the 2.45 GW Bloom Energy fuel cell deployment tied to that site faces fuel supply delays 14. The same report that tallied 9.8 GW of hyperscaler nuclear deals projected only 1 GW online before 2030 12.

ThreadD3.5

Large-Load Tariff Design & Co-Location Rules

The rules for plugging a data center into a wholesale market are being rewritten through FERC dockets and RTO filings. The Susquehanna case is the reference point.

Oct 1, 2026Data Center Frontier

FERC orders six operators to revise rules

FERC issued June 2026 show-cause orders to six grid operators requiring revised interconnection rules for loads above 50 MW, covering behind-the-meter generation, co-location and cost allocation 18.

Aug 15, 2026Data Center Knowledge

PJM: bring power or face cuts

PJM filed a tariff revision proposing a 'Bring Your Own New Capacity' mechanism requiring new large data center loads to supply qualifying capacity or face reliability backstop procurement 19.

Aug 13, 2026MTS Drops (FERC ER24-2172 annotated)

The Talen–Amazon order

FERC rejected Talen–Amazon's behind-the-meter arrangement at Susquehanna in November 2024, forcing a front-of-the-meter model by spring 2026 in which Talen supplies AWS via the PJM grid. The order directs PJM to create explicit transmission services for co-located loads 20.

Aug 26, 2026Measured AI

Susquehanna goes front-of-meter

Amazon's Susquehanna campus transitioned to a front-of-the-meter configuration in spring 2026 after the regulatory proceedings concluded 21.

Oct 4, 2026RTO Insider

California argues over 'large load'

CAISO and PG&E are in dispute over the definition of 'large loads' as AI data centers seek grid access in California 22.

ThreadD3.2 · D3.3

States, Moratoria & Utility Commissions

State actors moved faster than federal ones. Texas paused permits, North Carolina refused new gas, and Virginia's largest utility merger became a test of who speaks for ratepayers.

Sep 23, 2026Data Center Dynamics

Texas halts new permits

Governor Greg Abbott halted new data center permits pending completion of an ERCOT audit of grid capacity and reliability 28.

Oct 6, 2026Global Environmental Law Review

Two agencies, one pause

The pause combines the governor's 3 August ERCOT audit directive with a 21 September TCEQ freeze on new data center permitting until the audit is complete 29.

Sep 22, 2026Utility Dive

North Carolina rejects Duke turbines

Regulators rejected Duke Energy's request for a gas turbine facility, citing staggering cost and uncertain need 30.

Sep 23, 2026pv magazine USA

Arkansas ratepayers question Google–Entergy terms

Google's 'Fair Share Plus' arrangement with Entergy for a $4 billion West Memphis facility drew ratepayer concerns over redacted filings and trade-secret claims 31.

Oct 5, 2026Converge Digest

Kentucky doubles TeraWulf's power

TeraWulf doubled contracted power at its Muskie campus from 500 MW to 1 GW under an amended agreement with Kentucky Power, pulling the second phase from 2030 to 2029 32.

Sep 21, 2026Virginia Mercury

Reset the clock on Dominion–NextEra

Attorney General Jay Jones asked the State Corporation Commission to reset the 180-day review of the $67 billion merger after the companies filed supplemental documents 33. Legislators later said the window had closed to call a special session to extend the review 34.

Faraday's Take

The cited record does not show a shortage of buyers or of capital: in eight weeks it logs agreements covering several gigawatts of existing and uprated nuclear output 1,5,7 and billions in federal loans 6,9. What it shows instead is a queue of permissions, at FERC 18, in PJM 19, in Texas 28 and in state commissions 30,33, each deciding who pays to connect large loads. On this evidence, the projects that slip will be the ones that waited for those decisions, as Project Jupiter shows 13. The ones that hold their schedules will be the ones that bought capacity already on the grid.
